turn1.explanation: The unit responds to front-facing faces of furry mammals, specifically the layout of two eyes above a central nose or muzzle, as seen in foxes, cats, red pandas, hamsters, meerkats and ferrets. It likely responds to this face-like layout itself, which would explain the car.
turn1.evidence: 19 of the 20 top crops are close frontal views of small and medium furry mammals centered on the eyes and snout, with activations from 10 down to 7. The one exception, a Mercedes front at activation 9, shows two headlights above a central grille, a face-like arrangement that could trigger the same feature.
turn1.missing_data: Activations on frontal views of other face-like objects (car fronts, masks, outlets) compared with non-face car views and side views of animals, to tell a general face-layout detector apart from a mammal-face detector with an unrelated car response.
